question_text: A 21-year-old woman presents with right eye irritation, redness, and watery discharge. These symptoms started abruptly 4 days ago. She is on summer vacation and does not report any contacts with evidently ill patients. However, during the vacation, she frequently visited crowded places. The patient denies any other symptoms. At the presentation, the patient’s vital signs include: blood pressure 125/80 mm Hg, heart rate 75/min, respiratory rate 14/min, and temperature 36.7℃ (98℉). The physical examination shows conjunctival injection, watery discharge, and mild follicular transformation of the conjunctiva of the right eye. There are no corneal lesions. Ipsilateral preauricular lymph nodes are enlarged. Which of the following would be a proper medical therapy for this patient?
